heading.text: PROCEDURE 1 — COLD START-UP (from ambient, total plant shutdown)
Pre-requisites (all must be confirmed before proceeding):

paragraphs.text: ▶  PHASE 1: COOLING WATER AND UTILITIES START-UP (0–30 minutes)
Step 1.1   Start cooling water circulation pumps P-901A (duty). Confirm discharge pressure 4.0 ± 0.2 barg.
✓ Verify: CW supply pressure PT-901 = 3.8–4.2 barg; no vibration on pump casing
Step 1.2   Open CW isolation valves to E-301, E-501, E-502, E-701 acid coolers progressively (allow 2 minutes each).
✓ Verify: CW flow established to each cooler — confirm via local flow indicators
Step 1.3   Start BFW pump P-201A (duty). Set LIC-201 to maintain WHB drum level at 50 ± 5%.
✓ Verify: LT-201 reading stable 45–55%; no high-pressure steam generation yet — drum is cold
Step 1.4   Confirm instrument air ring main pressure 7.0 ± 0.3 barg. Confirm N₂ blanket to product tanks active.
✓ Verify: V-301 IA receiver pressure ≥ 7.0 barg; both product tanks show N₂ flow on local rotameters
▶  PHASE 2: ACID CIRCUIT PRIMING (30–90 minutes)
Step 2.1   Start DT acid circulating pump P-301A. Confirm AIC-501 not yet in auto — DT acid concentration monitoring only.
✓ Verify: P-301A running; LT-301 stable 40–60%; no air flow yet
Step 2.2   Start IPAT acid circulating pump P-501A. Confirm AT-501 reading 98.0–98.5 wt%.
⚠ CAUTION: If AT-501 < 97.5 wt%, do NOT proceed — top up with 98.5% make-up acid until target is achieved
Step 2.3   Start FAT acid circulating pump P-502A. Confirm AT-502 reading 98.0–98.5 wt%.
Step 2.4   Open dilution water FCV-501 and FCV-502 to approximately 20% output (approximately 45 L/h each). Set AIC-501 and AIC-502 to AUTO.
✓ Verify: AIC-501/502 in AUTO; water flow confirmed on FT-501/502
▶  PHASE 3: MAIN AIR BLOWER START AND CATALYST PRE-HEAT (90–180 minutes)
Step 3.1   Check blower K-301A anti-surge valve in OPEN position. Start K-301A at minimum speed (26 Hz / 50% VFD).
✓ Verify: K-301A running; discharge pressure 0.1–0.2 barg; no vibration; air flow FT-201 > 4,000 Nm³/h
Step 3.2   Slowly increase K-301A VFD speed to achieve air flow of 5,000 Nm³/h (approximately 57% speed). Maintain this flow for catalyst pre-heating.
✓ Verify: FT-201 = 4,800–5,200 Nm³/h; AT-301 (moisture) < 0.1 g/Nm³

⛔ WARNING: Do NOT proceed to ignition if AT-301 moisture reading exceeds 0.15 g/Nm³. High moisture entering the catalyst will cause permanent catalyst deactivation. Check DT acid concentration (target 94–96 wt%) and add make-up 98% acid if required.
Step 3.3   If start-up heater available: energise start-up gas heater to warm converter catalyst to 400°C (Pass 1 inlet). This step takes approximately 90 minutes.
✓ Verify: TT-401 (Pass 1 inlet) reading ≥ 400°C (minimum for sulfur ignition); confirm all 4 pass temperatures rising uniformly
⚠ CAUTION: If TT-401 fails to reach 400°C in 180 minutes, check heater operation and contact Process Engineer before proceeding
▶  PHASE 4: SULFUR IGNITION AND INITIAL COMBUSTION (duration 15–30 minutes)
⛔ WARNING: Confirm all 12 start-up permissives P-01 through P-12 are GREEN on DCS before initiating ignition.
Step 4.1   Confirm ESD system in armed state (all SIS logic energised, solenoids energised, trip functions active).
✓ Verify: DCS SIS status: all SIF armed; no bypasses active
Step 4.2   Open SDV-E01 (sulfur block valve) slowly — DCS command. Position feedback confirmed OPEN.
✓ Verify: SDV-E01 open position feedback on DCS
Step 4.3   Set FIC-101 to MANUAL mode. Gradually open FCV-101 to 10% output — targeting approximately 136 kg/h sulfur flow (10% of design).
✓ Verify: FT-101 reading 120–150 kg/h; TT-201 (furnace T) begins rising within 2 minutes
⚠ CAUTION: If furnace temperature does not begin rising within 3 minutes of sulfur admission, close FCV-101 immediately and purge for 10 minutes with air before re-attempting ignition
Step 4.4   Confirm stable combustion: TT-201 rising and AT-201 (SO₂) reading > 8 vol%.
✓ Verify: TT-201 > 700°C and rising; AT-201 > 8 vol%
Step 4.5   Switch FIC-101 to AUTO (cascade from Governor). Set Master Load to 10%.
✓ Verify: DCS Master Load = 10%; FIC-101 and FIC-201 in AUTO cascade
▶  PHASE 5: LOAD RAMP TO DESIGN (2–4 hours)
Step 5.1   Increase Master Load from 10% to 50% at rate of 5% per 10 minutes (maximum ramp rate). Monitor TT-401 through TT-408 continuously.
✓ Verify: All converter pass temperatures trending smoothly; TT-402 (Pass 1 outlet) must not exceed 610°C during ramp
⚠ CAUTION: If TT-402 approaches 605°C during ramp, pause load increase for 15 minutes until temperatures stabilise
Step 5.2   At 50% load: confirm AT-403 (stack SO₂) < 500 mg/Nm³. Continue ramp to 80%.
✓ Verify: AT-403 < 500 mg/Nm³; all absorption tower levels stable; AT-501/502 = 98.0–98.5 wt%
Step 5.3   At 80% load: confirm WHB steam generation established. Set PIC-202 to AUTO for steam export.
✓ Verify: FT-202 (steam flow) > 6,000 kg/h; PT-202 = 40 ± 1 barg; PIC-202 in AUTO
Step 5.4   At 80%: confirm all acid loops stabilised. Transition AIC-501 and AIC-502 from MANUAL trim to full AUTO.
✓ Verify: Both AIC loops in AUTO; concentrations stable ± 0.1 wt%
Step 5.5   Continue ramp to 100% load at same ramp rate. At 100%: declare Normal Operation.
✓ Verify: AT-403 < 300 mg/Nm³; TT-402 ≤ 600°C; AT-501/502 = 98.0–98.5 wt%; PT-202 = 40 barg; All DCS loops in AUTO
⚠ CAUTION: Complete start-up log entry; notify Shift Supervisor; schedule first product sample to laboratory within 30 min of reaching 100% load

paragraphs.text: ⛔ WARNING: Planned Shutdown must be authorised by the Shift Supervisor and notified to the Process Engineer and HSE department at least 1 hour before commencement.
▶  PHASE 1: LOAD REDUCTION (0–90 minutes)
Step S.1   Set Master Load to 80%. Confirm stable operation at 80% for 15 minutes.
✓ Verify: All loops stable; AT-403 < 300 mg/Nm³
Step S.2   Set Master Load to 60%. Continue monitoring converter temperatures and stack SO₂.
✓ Verify: TT-402 < 580°C; AT-403 < 400 mg/Nm³
⚠ CAUTION: If AT-403 > 400 mg/Nm³ at 60% load, reduce to 50% and notify HSE
Step S.3   Set Master Load to 50% (minimum stable turndown). Confirm 20 minutes stable operation.
✓ Verify: AT-403 < 480 mg/Nm³; all loops stable
Step S.4   Set Master Load to 0% (FIC-101 demand → 0). FIC-101 closes FCV-101. Confirm SDV-E01 closes automatically on zero flow.
✓ Verify: FT-101 = 0 kg/h; TT-201 begins to fall; AT-201 SO₂ begins to fall
▶  PHASE 2: FURNACE PURGE AND COOLING (90–240 minutes)
Step S.5   Continue K-301A air blower at 50% speed for air purge of furnace and converter. Minimum 30-minute air purge after sulfur cutoff.
✓ Verify: AT-201 (SO₂) < 1 vol% after 30 minutes of purge
⚠ CAUTION: Do NOT stop air blower until SO₂ < 1 vol% — residual SO₂ must be cleared before duct entry
Step S.6   Once TT-201 < 200°C, progressively reduce blower speed to 30% and maintain for natural cooling.
✓ Verify: TT-201 declining; TT-401 (converter) declining below 200°C
Step S.7   Maintain WHB BFW flow (LIC-201 in AUTO) until drum pressure PT-202 < 5 barg. Then close BFW isolation and drain steam circuit under Process Engineer supervision.
✓ Verify: PT-202 < 5 barg before BFW isolation; steam drum vented
⚠ CAUTION: Critical: BFW must remain on until pressure < 5 barg to prevent dry-fire during heat soak
▶  PHASE 3: ACID CIRCUIT DRAIN AND ISOLATION (240–360 minutes)
Step S.8   Transfer excess product acid from IPAT and FAT sumps to product storage tank TK-701. Confirm LT-701 < 80% (product tank).
✓ Verify: Transfer pump flow confirmed; LT-701 < 80%
Step S.9   Stop acid circulating pumps P-501A and P-502A. Close all acid isolation valves. Drain sumps to designated acid sump collection.
✓ Verify: No acid flow in absorption towers; all drain valves confirmed closed
Step S.10   Stop K-301A blower. Isolate air inlet. Complete shutdown log.
✓ Verify: K-301A stopped; all flows at zero; DCS confirms plant in "shutdown" state

NOTE: Post-shutdown: the plant remains a Major Hazard site even when shutdown. All entry to vessels or confined spaces requires a confined space entry permit, gas testing (O₂ > 19.5%; SO₂ < 0.5 ppm), and SCBA standby.
